title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a scoped seed load refuses a natural key a NULL-organization row holds instead of inserting a twin
body:
Fixes #24301

Clause-②: no (narrowing) (a seed load that inserted a twin now refuses that row; owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue)

Leg B of #24282 (leg A landed as PR #24325, `51ad8e4fb`). Dispatched by the `domain:engine` seat 1 (`session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`, claim comment 6251425947); this dev session is `session_01HsiLAicj3hYCseWnNxYkCj`.

## What changes

An organization-scoped seed load (`SeedLoaderService` with `config.organizationId`, in `upsert` or `ignore` mode) now refuses a seed record whose natural key a row with NULL `organization_id` already holds. Before, the scoped pre-load (`loadExistingRecords`) read `organization_id = ORG` only, the NULL holder was invisible, `decideWriteAction` answered `insert`, and a twin carrying the organization landed beside the unowned row, with 0 errors and nothing logged.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`, the two functions the claim names and the pre-load call site:

- **`loadExistingRecords`** takes an optional `unownedHolders` map. When the caller passes it on a scoped load, a second read, `where: { organization_id: null }` under the system context, fills it with every key held by a row that has no organization and that this organization does not hold. Those rows are never put in the returned map, so no caller ever matches one as the organization's own. The NULL read keeps only rows whose `organization_id` really is null, so another organization's row stays invisible whatever a driver answers. A failed read follows the existing #8896 rule (a missing table is empty, anything else propagates).
- **`decideWriteAction`** gains an optional `unownedHolders` parameter and a `refuse` answer: in `upsert` / `ignore`, an unmatched key held by an unowned row is `refuse`, never `insert` (a twin) and never `update`/`skip` against it (adoption). The organization's own row always wins over an unowned one.
- **The scoped caller** (`loadDataset`) asks for the holders only on a scoped upsert/ignore, and asks `decideWriteAction` once per record after reference resolution and before both write paths (the batched one and the self-referencing sequential `writeRecord`). A `refuse` becomes a per-row error through the existing path: `errored++`, `errors.push`, `allErrors.push`, logged at `error` once per dataset, then `continue`. The rest of the dataset still loads.

The refusal reuses `ReferenceResolutionError` unchanged: `field: 'organization_id'`, `targetObject` the seeded object itself, `targetField` the natural key, `attemptedValue` the key's value, and a message naming the object, the record, the key, the holding row's id, that it has no organization, and the remedy (`os migrate organization-ownership`, then `--apply`, then re-run the seed). No spec schema changes.

Nothing else moves: the two rechecks (`writeBatchPartial`'s retry and `writeOne`'s) are not passed the map, so they read the organization's rows exactly as before. No adoption, no migration, and `seed-replayer` / `@objectstack/verify` are not touched.

## Mechanism hypotheses, measured

- **M1 (reproduction): holds.** Real `SqlDriver` on a better-sqlite3 file, real `ObjectQL`, real `SeedLoaderService`; two `tw_event` rows and one `tw_task` row planted through the driver with `organization_id` NULL. On the unfixed loader (and again on the ablated build, below), the scoped load inserted all 5 seed rows: `tw_event` 2 → 5 and `tw_task` 1 → 3, a twin for each of the 3 NULL-held keys, 0 refusals. The fully stamped control already loaded with 0 inserts. With the fix: `tw_event` 2 → 3 and `tw_task` 1 → 2 (only the unheld keys), 3 named refusals, the unowned rows byte-identical.
- **H1 (the lookup): holds, with one change of shape.** The NULL holders are read by a second query and kept apart from the organization's rows, instead of widening the one scoped query (a `$or` would also break every engine double that refuses an operator key). Measured on SQLite (file), on the memory driver and on a live Postgres 16 (a local cluster started for the run and stopped after; the pin file temporarily ran the same four scenarios on `client: 'pg'`): `{ organization_id: null }` matched exactly the NULL rows on all three, and another organization's row holding the same key stayed invisible (this organization got its own row, the other was untouched). The permanent pin runs SQLite only: `check:driver-memory-census` refuses a new `@objectstack/driver-memory` consumer, and a Postgres case would need the live-dialect skip machinery the runtime suite does not carry.
- **H2 (the refusal): holds.** A per-row error through the existing path; never a silent skip, never a thrown abort (the unheld rows still load), never an adoption (`engine.update` is never called on the holder).
- **H3 (the three callers): refined.** The pre-load refuses. The two rechecks do **not** treat a NULL-held key as present: their question is "did an earlier attempt of this load commit this row?", and such a row carries the organization, so taking an unowned row for one would mis-attribute it (its id would land in the reference map and the seed-settlement report). They keep reading this organization's rows only, and a refused row never reaches the insert buffer they guard. Pinned: on a retried batch the one recheck read is `organization_id = ORG` and no insert payload ever carries a held key; on the `writeOne` degradation the same per row.

## Pins

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-null-organization-holder.test.ts` (8 tests, a fake whose `where` reads `{ f: null }` as IS NULL): upsert and ignore refuse and insert the rest; the organization's own row wins; `update` mode is unchanged and makes no NULL read; the self-referencing path refuses; the `writeBatchPartial` retry recheck and the `writeOne` recheck; an unscoped load makes no NULL read and still matches the unowned row.
- `packages/runtime/src/seed-loader-null-organization-holder-real-driver.integration.test.ts` (6 tests, real SQLite file). It lives in `packages/runtime` because `@objectstack/objectql` depends on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, so the loader's package cannot reach a real engine without a cycle; this is where the existing real-driver seed pins live. It covers: row counts before and after with the named error's content (object, record index, key, holder id, the remedy's command) and the cascade (the two tasks' links to refused events are reported as dropped, never pointed at an unowned row); a fully stamped database loads with 0 inserts and 0 errors; the cross-tenant guarantee; an unscoped load unchanged; and every scoped caller: the per-organization replay through the production replayer a walled `AppPlugin` boot registers, and the walled install and reseed through the request `runInlineSeed` builds for both.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: 3 rows from `node scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write` for the new test's fake (the gate's own instruction for new pinned coverage). It is outside the claim's file list and is the gate's mechanical ledger.

## Verification (head `7cfdef02`, after merging `origin/main` `a2a3777b`)

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' --filter @objectstack/runtime build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`, the new test is in the test-layer program and clean).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` (before the merge): 245 files passed, 3 skipped; 20649 tests passed.
- Runtime seed suites (`src/seed*`, `app-plugin.seed*`, `autonumber-seed*`, `standalone-stack-seeder*`): 16 files, 158 tests passed. The two new files pass on the merged head (8 and 6 tests).
- **Ablation (one line):** `if (unowned) return { action: 'refuse', ... }` gated off through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` marker present in 2 dist files. Unit file 5 failed / 3 passed; real-driver file 4 failed / 6 passed (`tw_event` length 5, not 3; inserted 5, not 2). Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, blob hash equal to HEAD, rebuilt, marker absent from all 24 dist files, tree clean, real-driver file 10/10 green.
- Derived gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` with no paths on `7cfdef02` derived 73 commands; all 73 ran and exited 0, and `--ran` reconciles them: "73 derived famil(ies) accounted for, 73 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero, all 73 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)". Readings on the way there: `check:engine-double-contract` asked for the ledger rows above; `check:query-options-erasure` reddened on an untyped options bag (now `EngineQueryOptions`); `check:driver-memory-census` refused a memory-driver consumer (removed); `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needed its pinned fixture commit fetched on this shallow clone. `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:type-check-debt` were re-run alone with a longer budget after a 280 s cap killed them (exit 124), and both exit 0. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `test:repo` are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- `update` mode is unchanged: it never inserts, so it makes no twin, and a NULL-held key is skipped as before (no NULL read is made). `insert` / `replace` modes are unchanged too (they never pre-load).
- A refused row also has its deferred references reported as dropped by pass 2, as every other failed write does.
